summary: Phase 4 review-fix batch: the defects two independent reviews found in this campaign's unreleased work, each reproduced with a test observed failing before its fix - two partitioned survivors could both be promoted and give one pool two masters, a promotion could power off a reachable healthy master, two hosts could run concurrent promotions, the pool's virtual-machine owner records still moved during an authority freeze, a master change handed to a host that then died killed the pool permanently, a member's self-claim could take the pool while a member-first Controller replacement deadlocked at enrolment, a join invitation outlived its window after a Controller restart and a scrubbed one was redelivered empty, a host could leave its pool with no report from the master, the management-network rollback used the wall clock and failed exactly in the cut-off case, apply and rollback destroyed the management bridge and cut off every guest on it, a change could be confirmed on an observation that never crossed it, a failed rollback reported nothing, a spec was never checked against the host, re-staging with a different configuration replayed the old one, maintenance did not block starting a local-storage guest or waking a suspended one, libvirt autostart returned guests to a drained host after a reboot, a join reported failed while the master held a ready membership row, the host-local join path destroyed a Controller-driven record, the invitation stayed at rest on the joining host, a clustered-storage apply could move the records during a freeze, the promote route could not drive a current Nex Core and a performed cancellation read as a failure, and the rollback timer died with the agent - plus the operator consent, reported fields and unit-file change those fixes required

guide.reason: Operator-visible behaviour changed on five pages. Pool authority and recovery: a promotion can power off more than one host, so the acknowledgement names every host on the list and is dropped when the list changes; an unreachable ready member now blocks a promotion unless the same promotion fences it, and a host already running a promotion blocks it too; a new Resume on the current master path recovers a master change whose target died, with the conditions Nex Core enforces and the fact that its result is an outcome rather than a failure; the fence trust property (any ready member can power off any profiled host) and the 1 MiB authority-copy ceiling are stated; and the review's blocking findings are named with the fact that they were found before release and fixed with regressions. Host maintenance: a table of exactly what is refused and what is allowed while drained - local-storage starts and wakes refused, reboot and force-reboot allowed, libvirt autostart suppressed and restored on exit, the libvirt hook refusing a manual virsh start on a master, and the honest limit that it does not on a member - plus the staleness of a member's copy of the flag. Change a host's management network: the bridge is reconfigured in place rather than bounced, so a VM on the management bridge is no longer disturbed, stated explicitly as designed and unverified on a real host; the new stage-time refusals; the rollback no longer reading the clock and what that means for a host with a wrong RTC or a suspended host; the limit that the rollback needs the agent running, with Restart=always and the stopped-or-masked hole; and the NIC-omission limit. Join a pool: only pre-admission stages can report a failed join, the retry past the invitation's window is correct and why, the expired-uncollected message, and where the invitation is scrubbed on both sides. Manage Nex Controller: adding the member first to a replacement Controller now works. Every Verification section keeps and extends its statement that nothing here has been walked through natively or in a browser for this build.

api.reason: Both sides are implemented in this batch. Client-facing Controller API: POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master/promote gains a required, non-empty fence_host_ids - exactly the set the candidate's own fresh preflight named, each host once, sorted by the Controller so the same set typed in another order replays and forwarded verbatim - with two new 400 refusals and host lookup failed added to its 500; POST /api/v1/pools/{id}/master/cancel gains optional fence_confirmed and fence_host_ids, accepted both or neither, which Nex Core uses only to resume a hand-off whose target has died; the pool-level last_transfer and last_promotion gain reason, carrying Core's sentence for an operation that succeeded so a performed cancellation is never rendered as a failed transfer; and each member's fence object gains credential_version. Controller-to-Core and host-to-Controller: PoolTransferStatus gains handed_off, always present, the source's own durable answer to whether it has signed the authority away; cancellable is now always present on PoolTransferStatus and PoolPromotionStatus; the promotion verdict's fence_host_ids and each probed host's blocks, fence_recorded, fence_usable and fence_unusable_reason are the structural form of a promotion that fences more than one host; the pool-promote command carries fence_host_ids and the pool-transfer transfer-cancel action carries fence_confirmed and fence_host_ids. Behaviour within existing contracts: adoption of a reported master is now evidence-gated and fails closed, with an equal-generation reconnect arm; POST /api/v1/agent/enroll accepts one additional evidence shape for the pool identity is held wait; an uncollected expired pool-join is failed terminally with a new sentence on GET /api/v1/operations rather than redelivered empty; a pool-join result can report needs_attention where it reported failed at the admission stage; vm-power start, wake and vm-create can now be refused with the existing maintenance sentence on local-storage guests; and the clustered-storage apply and verify-fence actions can now carry the existing retryable frozen-authority sentence. No new route, command kind or capability. The management-network contract is unchanged: its two new record fields are host-local and are not reported. The packaging change in this batch carries API impact none on its own: both systemd units move from Restart=on-failure to Restart=always, which is a unit-file setting with no endpoint, field, command or report shape behind it. It is here because it is the other half of the management-network rollback fix - every rollback trigger runs inside that process - and its operator consequence is written into the management-network guide as a limit: the rollback needs the agent running, a crash or an out-of-memory kill is now covered, and a unit deliberately stopped or masked between applying and the deadline still arms nothing. Its own checks are tests/test_agent_service.py and tests/test_core_local_package.py, which assert the setting and name the rollback window as the reason.

roadmap.reason: These are defect fixes inside Phase 4 work the published board already shows as in progress. Nothing moves to built, no feature is added and no claim on the board changes. The Phase 4 native acceptance gate that would move anything is still outstanding, and one of the stated reasons it is outstanding - that no real fence has ever executed - is unchanged by this batch.

state.reason: Every durable field this batch adds or changes belongs to a host, and every one of them is already replicated or re-adopted from the host's own report. No Controller table, column or file gains a copy of anything pool-scoped: the Controller's only new state is an in-memory timestamp of when it last swept for expired join invitations, which is a rate limiter and not a record, and the required fence_host_ids it stores is the operator's own confirmed request payload in the existing managed_resources replay row, which Nex Core recomputes and re-checks before it powers anything off. The two management-network fields are host-local and are deliberately not reported at all, because a fresh Controller needs neither: they are how the host measures its own rollback window. The two systemd unit files add no state.
state.record: Pool authority and promotion: the pool master's own <state-dir>/pool-peer.json. Transfer.Fences replaces Transfer.Fence and holds one verified fence proof per excluded host, each bound to pool, host, operation and authority generation and reused on retry while fresh; Transfer.FenceAgreed holds the set the operator confirmed, re-checked against Core's freshly computed set at the preflight stage and again inside the fence stage; Transfer.HandedOff was already durable and is now reported as handed_off; SelfFence and Restricted are unchanged in kind. PoolMember.Fence and PoolMember.FenceCredentialVersion live in the pool master's durable membership and are replicated with it, so a promoted master inherits every profile and a fresh Controller re-adopts all of it from Inventory.Managed.Membership. Maintenance: the drain flag stays a field of that same membership record, and a member reads it from the stored signed authority replica rather than from any Controller copy. Join: the joining host's own pool-peer.json pending-join record, from which the invitation is now scrubbed once the admission stage completes; the join stage itself is reported as Inventory.Managed.Join and re-adopted from it. Management network: <state-dir>/management-network.json gains boot_id and applied_uptime_ns, both host-local, both omitempty, neither reported - a record written without them behaves exactly as before, and the stage, spec, snapshot and any running deadline continue to reach a fresh Controller through Inventory.management_network. libvirt autostart: the managed journal remains the one durable record of the desired value, and the drained or restricted suppression is applied on top of it and never written back, so leaving maintenance restores exactly what the operator asked for.
state.record_note: The Controller-side fixes in this batch (adoption evidence, the enrolment evidence shape, the join invitation sweep, the redelivery rule, the unilateral-leave rule, the promote and cancel bodies, reason and credential_version) add no durable Controller state at all. They remove or refuse things: an adoption that had no evidence, an invitation past its window, a command redelivered empty, a pool move no host reported. The one new Controller field, joinScrubbed, is in memory and is re-earned after a restart.

verification.method: IMPLEMENTED; NOTHING NATIVE OR IN A BROWSER. Two independent reviews of this campaign's unreleased work were carried out on 2026-09-19 - one on Nex Core's authority, promotion and fence paths, one on the Controller relays, slices S1 to S3 and the architecture invariant. The invariant review's verdict was that the invariant holds, with authentication, authorization, secret handling and injection clean, and five blocking findings; the authority review's verdict was that the work was not safe to take into a native run as it stood, with three reproduced findings. Every blocking finding of both reviews is fixed in this batch, each with a regression written and observed failing first; the observed pre-fix output is recorded per defect in docs/BUG_LEDGER.md entries BUG-0333 through BUG-0353. Every guard added was mutation-tested: reverting it makes its own test fail. Go race suites: go test -race -count=1 -timeout 40m ./... - all packages ok, internal/controller 291.025s, internal/agent 17.972s, internal/vmhost 12.813s, internal/localcore 10.169s, internal/protocol 1.043s. Named regressions and their files are listed per entry in the bug ledger. Web: npm run typecheck clean and npm test green across every suite including pool-promotion, pool-authority and pool-members, nothing skipped. Python: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' - 373 tests, OK, including tests/test_agent_service.py and tests/test_core_local_package.py asserting Restart=always on both units and naming the management-network rollback window as the reason. Offline contract checks: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_api_contract.py' - 73 tests, OK - and python3 scripts/generate_api.py --check. Documentation gate: python3 scripts/check_docs.py --worktree and --all. Privacy: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_repository_privacy.py'. CI coverage confirmed by inspection, not edited: .github/workflows/phase1.yml and .gitea/workflows/phase1.yml both trigger on push to '**' (lines 2-5) and on pull_request (line 6), and both run go test -race -timeout 20m ./... at line 29, python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v at line 53 and npm --prefix web run test at line 70, so every regression above runs on both runners and no workflow change was needed. NOT executed, recorded as outstanding: no native multi-host run of anything in this batch; NO REAL FENCE HAS EVER RUN, so every promotion, every multi-host exclusion and the fence-backed resume are proven only against a test double injected at the poolFenceVerify seam; TestManagementNetworkNetns has still never executed anywhere, so the in-place bridge reconfiguration, the guest taps staying attached, the DHCP transitions and the real rollback are proven only in the sense that the tests show which commands run and that the destroying ones do not; a management-network confirmation that legitimately counts cannot be produced in-process, because every in-process lab runs on loopback; the agent-side wiring that applies the suppressed libvirt autostart flag needs a real libvirt and has no end-to-end test; and no browser review of the promotion dialog's fence list, the resume dialog, the maintenance table's behaviour or any Phase 4 screen at 360 px has been carried out.
